intro: Choose one answer for each question. 8 marks.
items: 1. Atomic number is the number of: A neutrons; B protons; C protons + neutrons; D shells.
B. Proton number identifies the element.
2. Which particle is negative? A proton; B neutron; C electron; D nucleus.
C. An electron has charge -1 and is outside the nucleus.
3. Across a period, first ionization energy generally: A increases; B decreases; C stays constant; D becomes zero.
A. Greater effective nuclear attraction generally makes electron removal harder.
4. Which scientist left gaps while arranging elements mainly by atomic mass? A Bohr; B Moseley; C Mendeleev; D Chadwick.
C. Modern ordering uses atomic number.
5. Which conducts when molten but not as a solid? A CO2; B KCl; C CH4; D O2.
B. Molten KCl has mobile ions; solid KCl has fixed ions.
6. Which is polyatomic? A Na+; B Cl-; C NH4+; D Mg2+.
C. Ammonium contains several bonded atoms with overall charge +1.
7. Which bond is non-polar? A H-Cl; B N-N; C O-H; D C-O.
B. Identical nitrogen atoms share equally.
8. A lilac flame suggests: A Na+; B K+; C Li+; D Cu2+.
B. Potassium produces the lilac flame in the course examples.

intro: Give concise definitions with the key scientific words. 8 marks.
items: 9. Define isotope.
Atoms of the same element (same proton number) [1] with different neutron numbers [1].
10. Define first ionization energy.
Energy required to remove one electron [1] from an isolated gaseous atom [1].
11. Define electronegativity.
Ability of a bonded atom [1] to attract shared/bonding electrons [1].
12. Define ionic bond.
Electrostatic attraction [1] between oppositely charged ions [1].
13. A particle has 17 protons, 18 neutrons and 18 electrons. Find Z, A and its charge.
Z=17 [1]; A=17+18=35 [1]; charge=17-18=-1 [1]. It is a chloride ion.
14. Isotopes have masses 10 u (20%), 11 u (30%) and 12 u (50%). Calculate the average atomic mass and explain why it is not a whole number.
Fractions 0.20, 0.30, 0.50 [1]; weighted expression 10(0.20)+11(0.30)+12(0.50) [1]; 11.3 u [1]. It is a weighted average of different isotopes, not the mass number of a single atom [1].

intro: Give the order or comparison AND the reason. 6 marks.
items: 15. Arrange F, Cl, Br and I by increasing atomic radius. Explain.
F < Cl < Br < I [1]. Down the group, extra occupied electron shells increase radius [1].
16. Which is larger, Na or Na+? Explain.
Na [1]. Formation of Na+ removes its outer electron and occupied outer shell; remaining electrons are more tightly held [1].
17. Why does atomic radius generally decrease from left to right across a period?
Nuclear charge/proton number increases [1] while added electrons occupy the same main shell, so stronger effective attraction pulls them closer [1].

intro: One mark per correct formula/name. 10 marks.
items: 18. Write formulas: (a) aluminium oxide; (b) magnesium phosphate; (c) iron(III) chloride; (d) ammonium sulfate; (e) carbon tetrachloride.
(a) Al2O3; (b) Mg3(PO4)2; (c) FeCl3; (d) (NH4)2SO4; (e) CCl4. One mark each. Balance charge for ionic substances; use prefixes for molecular compounds.
19. Name: (a) FeS; (b) Mg(ClO3)2; (c) PCl5; (d) N2O5; (e) CoCl2.6H2O.
(a) iron(II) sulfide; (b) magnesium chlorate; (c) phosphorus pentachloride; (d) dinitrogen pentoxide; (e) cobalt(II) chloride hexahydrate. One mark each.

intro: Show all lone pairs and any overall charge. 9 marks.
items: 20. Draw NH3, H2O and one resonance contributor for CO3^2-.

NH3: three N-H bonds [1], one N lone pair [1], correct total 8 electrons/complete H duets and N octet [1]. H2O: two O-H bonds [1], two O lone pairs [1], total 8 electrons and correct octet/duets [1]. CO3^2-: central C with one double and two single C-O bonds [1], correct O lone pairs (2 on double-bonded O; 3 on each single-bonded O) [1], brackets and overall 2- charge [1]. Total 24 electrons. See diagrams in the revision section.
21. Explain why solid KBr does not conduct but molten KBr does.
Solid: ions exist [1] but are fixed in a lattice/not free to move [1]. Molten: ions are mobile [1] and carry charge through the substance [1]. Do not say there are no ions in the solid.
22. Compare how ionic and covalent bonds form.
Ionic formation involves electron transfer [1], producing positive and negative ions held by electrostatic attraction [1]. Covalent bonding involves sharing [1] electron pairs between atoms [1].
23. EN(C)=2.6 and EN(O)=3.4. Find the difference and classify the C-O bond.
Difference=|3.4-2.6|=0.8 [1]; polar covalent under the supplied course convention [1]. Oxygen is partially negative.
24. Identify (a) radiation consisting of two protons and two neutrons; (b) radiation consisting of high-energy electromagnetic waves.
(a) alpha [1]; (b) gamma [1].
